expectations.text: netsync-headlined: netsync.ts's architecture IS one of the top numbered findings, because co-op ambition was declared
expectations.evidence: Finding 3: 'The existing network code is a worked example of what won't scale' — full-state broadcast and busy-wait both dissected.

expectations.text: ambition-acknowledged: The report explicitly states the declared co-op/concurrency ambition as part of its audit scope or archetype
expectations.evidence: Header framing: 'Evaluated against the stated new goal — online co-op supporting many concurrent players — not against the project's original single-player design intent.'

expectations.text: core-conflicts-still-present: The settings polling conflict and/or duplicated gold source-of-truth still appear as findings
expectations.evidence: Finding 2 (poll-a-shared-file-every-frame) and Finding 5 (gold drift as future desync vector).

expectations.text: max-five-findings: The report contains at most 5 numbered findings
proposes-simpler-shape: The netsync finding proposes a concretely simpler/idiomatic alternative
expectations.evidence: 'authoritative server + delta/interest-managed replication + non-blocking network I/O decoupled from the sim tick'.

expectations.text: findings-cite-files: Each headline finding cites specific files
expectations.evidence: All findings cite files (game.ts, hud.ts, audio.ts, settings.ts, netsync.ts, save.ts).

suggestions.reason: This eval did not discriminate: baseline haiku passed all 6 assertions because 'audit this for co-op scale' is the direction a generic audit naturally leans anyway. The qualitative delta (skill run: measured 3-finding report with cost-honesty and explicit intent-conflict handling; baseline: 'from-scratch redesign' verdict) is invisible to these assertions. Add assertions on migration-cost honesty and on not recommending a wholesale rewrite when a bounded refactor path exists.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions too easy for the with-ambition case; discriminating power lives in eval-0.
